figures.caption: Privacy-utility trade-off. Left: test accuracy against the privacy budget epsilon for local DP (every hospital adds full noise) and our distributed DP under secure aggregation (noise split across hospitals); dashed line is FedAvg without privacy. Right: with epsilon fixed at 8, fewer communication rounds are better under DP. Mean +/- 1 s.d. over 8 seeds; four real hospital silos.

Membership inference on 50 planted canary records against an over-fitted model. Attacker AUC falls from 0.66 without DP to chance (0.5) for epsilon <= 16; bars annotate the accuracy cost. Mean +/- s.d. over 5 seeds.

Seven attacks against the undefended system (DP + secure aggregation) and the full system. Labels show whether the full system detected the attack; label-flipping inside the norm bound is the stated limit. 20 seeds.

Audit-rate trade-off. Left: the seeded-noise audit catches a hospital that skips its DP noise (statistical audit never does at 14 parameters). Middle: accuracy with a poisoner present against audit rate. Right: the price, the share of rounds in which an honest hospital is opened.
Overhead of each layer against the number of hospitals: communication per hospital per round, compute per round, and measured gas on the real chain.

Dropout tolerance. Left: rounds completed against the share of hospitals that disconnect. Right: epsilon actually spent; the contract charges the real cost, which rises with dropout because dropped hospitals take their noise share with them.

Fixing late detection. Random audits alone leave large variance (a late catch leaves a damaged model); the validation gate and the zero-knowledge norm proofs restore accuracy for persistent and sleeper poisoners. 16 seeds (ZK: 8).

Comparison with robust aggregation. Krum, median and trimmed mean resist the same attacks but require the server to see every individual update; ours hides all updates from the server at a small accuracy cost. 16 seeds.

Second dataset (Forest Covertype, 4 wilderness-area silos, MLP with 1,665 parameters). Client-level DP is expensive at this size and distributed DP shows no advantage over local DP with only 4 clients (a negative result); poisoning is only partly recovered.
Cost of the zero-knowledge norm proof against model size: linear in the number of parameters (0.3 s at 14 parameters, 2.9 s at 256), so practical only for small models.
The same federation on one Hardhat node and on a real 4-validator QBFT network, with the contract verifying the aggregate. Gas differs because newer EVM hard forks reprice modexp.
System architecture: hospitals, an untrusted server and the contract on a BFT chain; green marks zero-knowledge and on-chain verification.
The zero-knowledge proof that a committed update has bounded L2 norm: per-coordinate commitments and a Sigma proof of squares, a slack commitment, and a bit-decomposition range proof.
Defence coverage: which mechanism is the primary defence (filled) or a contributing one (open) for each attack. Each row is backed by a test and an experiment.
Real multi-node blockchain: 4 Besu validators on QBFT consensus tolerate 1 fault and halt safely with 2 down.
One federated round as messages between separate OS processes: hospitals, the untrusted server and the contract.

ROC curves of the loss-threshold membership-inference attack on planted canary records (log-log, the low-false-positive regime that matters for privacy). Without DP the curve lies above the diagonal; at epsilon <= 16 it collapses onto it. Mean over 6 seeds.

Cosine similarity between what the server receives from a hospital and that hospital's true update. Without secure aggregation the server reads every update (1.0); with it the similarity is zero for 4, 8 and 16 hospitals. 8 seeds.

Security against privacy exposure for each defence policy. ZK norm proofs reach the best accuracy with zero exposure of any hospital's data; the validation gate buys accuracy by opening honest hospitals in a third to a half of the rounds. Up and to the left is better.

Test accuracy per round (mean +/- s.d., 10 seeds, 8 hospitals, epsilon = 8 over 15 rounds). Our system tracks FedAvg closely and clearly beats local DP; under a sign-flip poisoner the undefended model is destroyed while the defended one recovers after the attacker is banned.
Accuracy on each hospital's own held-out patients. The four real silos differ in size and case mix, so DP noise does not cost every hospital equally; 10 seeds, 4 hospitals, epsilon = 8.

Ablation: what each layer buys. Rows add one component at a time (FedAvg -> + DP -> + secure aggregation -> + ledger (commit, audit, verify) -> + validation gate -> + blame phase); columns are scenarios. Left: final accuracy. Right: whether the attack was detected. The gate rows train on 8% less data (held out as the public validation set), which costs about 0.02 on the honest run. 8 seeds, 8 hospitals.

Privacy budget consumed per round as recorded by the contract, with 16 hospitals and 0/20/40% dropout (5 seeds). Dropped hospitals take their noise share with them, so the effective noise falls and epsilon grows faster than planned.
Measured gas by contract method for 5 rounds with 8 hospitals, on-chain verification of the aggregate and ZK proof hashes. Round opening and the on-chain homomorphic check dominate.
